s.g: A person who secretly watches and examines the actions of other individuals or organizations and gathers information on them (usually to gain an advantage).

(American football) A defensive player assigned to cover an offensive backfield player man-to-man when they are expected to engage in a running play, but the offensive player does not run with the ball immediately.

s.x: During the Cold War, Russia and America would each spy on each other for recon.

s.g: (transitive) To spot; to catch sight of; to espy.
s.x: I think I can spy that hot guy coming over here.

s.g: (transitive) To explore; to see; to view; inspect and examine secretly, as a country.
A camera, especially a webcam, used for covert surveillance.
The skills and techniques employed by spies.
An open-topped sports car; a roadster.

spying.f: present participle and gerund of spy

s.g: espionage; the act of secretly gathering information
The leader of a group of spies.
(Internet) Programs that surreptitiously monitor and report the actions of a computer user.
